findings.text: §12 says "vector_indexes carries those properties into the index creation statement", but `vector_indexes` is a `GraphSchema` property in `imas_codex/graph/schema.py:211` while the DDL that creates the index is `CREATE VECTOR INDEX ... FOR (n:{label}) ON n.{prop}` inside `GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes` (client.py:403), fed by `EXPECTED_VECTOR_INDEXES` (client.py:59) which is built from the GENERATED `imas_codex/graph/schema_context_data.py` (`VECTOR_INDEXES: dict[str, tuple[str, str]]`) produced by `scripts/gen_schema_context.py`; a fourth (filter-property) element changes the generated 2-tuple the client consumes, so the plan must extend the DDL owner and its generated feed, not only the schema property — as written it points the author at schema.py and `build_vector_search` and leaves the index-creation layer unnamed and un-accounted

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no section adds surface without depth; §9(a) removes a duplicate probe call and §9(b) collapses three DataAccess writers into one `persist_data_access(data_access)`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §12 threads filter properties into "the index creation statement" but names only `schema.py::vector_indexes`; the statement that actually creates the index is owned by `GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes` in `imas_codex/graph/client.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §12 adds "one schema annotation key" to a budget-of-zero family and names nothing it retires or merges, and does not state why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every implementable section names the mechanism it extends and the file that owns it (§11 `imas_codex/graph/profiles.py::resolve_neo4j`; §9 `imas_codex/remote/tools.py::probe_remote_environment` and `imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py`; §13 the §3 collision repair in the same `search_tools.py`; §12 `imas_codex/graph/vector_search.py::build_vector_search` and `imas_codex/graph/schema.py::vector_indexes`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the only interface-growth proposals are extensions of an existing owner (`build_vector_search` gains a pre-filter form; `resolve_neo4j` reorders an existing branch; `get_python_status` takes an already-resolved argument), each justified in its section.
